data.title: MOSHO: A Native Discrete Shark-Inspired Metaheuristic for Hardware-Aware Neural Architecture Search
data.description: arXiv:2610.33358v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hardware-aware neural architecture search (NAS) requires jointly optimizing predictive accuracy and device-specific latency over discrete search spaces. While multi-objective swarm optimizers show promise, continuous formulations such as the Multi-Objective White Shark Optimizer (MOWSO) can suffer from quantization noise when rounded to integer-encoded architecture vectors. To address this limitation, we propose MOSHO (Multi-Objective Shark Hunting Optimization), a native discrete metaheuristic that replaces continuous motion equations with discrete architecture-editing operators. MOSHO integrates adaptive operator scheduling, energy-regulated restarts, and deferred crowding-distance truncation to enhance exploration and search efficiency. On the merged NAS-Bench-201/HW-NAS-Bench benchmark across 18 contexts, MOSHO achieves a median normalized hypervolume of 0.9987 and IGD+ of 0.0064, yielding Pareto fronts competitive with NSGA-II while reducing search runtime by 96.4% (0.64 s vs. 17.72 s). These results demonstrate that tailored discrete search mechanisms can enable swarm optimizers to achieve high-quality multi-objective solution quality with substantially lower search cost in hardware-aware NAS.
data.author: Nazim Abdeerhmane Aouni, Zakaria Soualah Mohammed, Maroua Ogab, Nour El Imane Elbar, Rayane Rahmat Errahmane Smara, Billel Moussous, Adriane Anis Khaled, Malika Bessedik, Fatima Benbouzid Si Tayeb, Hadjer Benmeziane
